# UNKNOWN status: provider call timed out

> UNKNOWN is a payment status that means a Stripe API call timed out, so the charge may or may not have gone through.

_Part of [Payment status values](payment-status.md)_

When you send a charge request to Stripe, the network connection can time out before you receive a response. In that moment, Stripe may have processed the payment or it may not have—you genuinely don't know. Rather than guess and risk duplicating charges or losing legitimate ones, the payment record is created with status=UNKNOWN. A background job then periodically checks Stripe by [idempotency key](idempotency-key-matching.md) to find out what actually happened and update the payment to its real status. The fundamental rule: never retry a charge if the provider times out. Always query Stripe first to ask what happened to that specific idempotency key. [The resolve-unknown job](resolving-unknown-payments.md) runs every 5 minutes and keeps checking until it gets an answer.

**Look at:** [`PaymentStatus` in payment.model.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/payment.model.ts#L33) · [`Payment` in payment.model.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/payment.model.ts#L23)

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | `Payment.status column` | Stores the payment's current state as one of six values; set to UNKNOWN when Stripe times out, then updated to the real status by the resolve-unknown job once Stripe responds. |

## Watch out

- A timeout does not mean the charge failed—Stripe may have accepted it anyway. Retrying blindly risks duplicate charges.
- The `providerRef` (Stripe [`PaymentIntent`](../../../../packages/payments/internal/stripe/stripe.go#L32) id) may not be filled in when status is UNKNOWN; it gets set during resolution.
- UNKNOWN is not permanent. The resolve-unknown job will eventually discover the real status, which could be COMPLETED, FAILED, or something else.
- If the job cannot reach Stripe for 60 minutes, it gives up and leaves the payment in UNKNOWN—manual intervention is needed to escalate.
